title: Remember the links
hook: Asked 'why is there a puddle?', can you answer?

knows: reading short labels and comparing simple counts
doesNotKnow: that an explanation is the links between ideas, what causes what, so a test has to ask for those links rather than the words

misconception: If you can list the key words, you understand the explanation.
objective: Reconstruct an explicit cause-and-consequence chain without its source.

claims.text: Scenario, hook and prediction: Asked 'why is there a puddle?', can you answer? You can list 'cloud, rain, puddle'. Asked 'why is there a puddle?', can you answer? Correct option: Only if you learned the links. All fixture labels, example words, dates, task durations and file fields are stipulated exercise data.

claims.text: Listing tav, bix and rell does not say which turns which, so it cannot answer 'why does rell turn?'. Only the remembered links can. A list like cloud, rain, puddle is the same: words, not yet the explanation.
claims.source: Roediger & Karpicke (2006), Test-Enhanced Learning, Psychological Science 17(3),249–255, DOI10.1111/j.1467-9280.2006.01693.x; publisher abstract retrieved 2026-10-13: https://www.psychologicalscience.org/journals/psychological-science/j.1467-9280.2006.01693.x/ . Prose-passage experiments found delayed retention advantages for retrieval over restudy. This short exercise does not establish that effect for the learner. Fixture mappings and rules are explicit conventions, not empirical demonstrations. FC LH-1 (session 2, received by message): verified; see company/reviews/lifehacks-200/fact-check-LH1-2026-10-14.md. Logic on the stage: the covered card lists bix, rell, tav alphabetically with no arrows, so the list alone cannot answer 'What turns rell?'; only the studied links (tav turns bix, bix turns rell) can. No empirical effect is claimed in the text; the Roediger & Karpicke citation is background only.

claims.text: Stage: the card (tav, bix, rell; each arrow means “turns”) shows at the prediction and is covered after it (bix, rell, tav). Each answer box starts empty and cycles through fixed choices (What turns rell?: tav, bix, rell; What turns bix?: tav, rell, bix). Pressing each box once gives: Links 1 of 2. The readout “Words listed 3/3” stands for the check made with everything in view. Reveal sentences: You could list all three words. Both links came back: the words alone could not have given them.

claims.text: The explanation is the ordered links; an alphabetical list or a count drops the cause-and-result order.

recall.question: Your notes say: alarm rings, then you wake, then you catch the bus. Which check tests the explanation, not just the words?
options: Count how many of the events you remember
Rebuild the chain from cause to result
recall.why: The explanation is the ordered links; an alphabetical list or a count drops the cause-and-result order.
